Ghaith: Arabic, meaning 'rain' or 'life-giving rain', often with the sense of help and relief. Also spelled Ghayth.
Bryan: English form of Celtic Brian, probably from Old Irish 'high' or 'noble'. Made famous by the Irish king Brian Boru.
Joyce: English, from the Breton name Iodoc or Josse, meaning 'lord'. Later also read as 'joy'; used for both sexes in English.
Ilona: Hungarian form of Helen, from Greek, usually explained as 'torch' or 'shining light'. Popular across Central and Eastern Europe.
Kyan: Modern name of uncertain origin; possibly a variant of Ryan or Kian, or of Persian origin meaning 'king'. Probably a creative modern spelling.
Flavie: French feminine form of Latin Flavius, meaning 'golden-haired' or 'yellow-haired'. Related to Flavia.
Israe: Variant spelling of Arabic Israa, meaning 'night journey', referring to the Prophet Muhammad's night journey in Islamic tradition.
Yunus: Arabic and Turkish form of Jonah, the prophet swallowed by a great fish. Likely linked to Hebrew 'dove'.
Leana: Modern name, probably a variant of Leanne or Liana, or a short form of Eleana. Origin uncertain; possibly linked to Helen or to Gaelic 'lover'.
Firdaous: Arabic Firdaws, meaning 'paradise' or the highest garden of paradise, itself borrowed from Persian. Also spelled Firdaus.
Safouan: Arabic Safwan, meaning 'clear, pure, rocky smooth stone'. Borne by a companion of the Prophet Muhammad; Maghrebi French spelling.
Kadiatou: West African (Fula, Guinean) form of Khadija, the Prophet Muhammad's first wife. From Arabic, often read as 'early-born child'.
Lyano: Modern coined name, probably a variant of Liano or Lyan, or a masculine form of Liana. Origin uncertain.
Aimée: French, meaning 'beloved', the past participle of aimer 'to love'. From Latin amare.
Faris: Arabic, meaning 'horseman' or 'knight'. A common name across the Arabic-speaking world.
Metehan: Turkish, probably from Mete, the first Hun emperor, and han 'ruler'. Roughly 'ruler Mete'.
Chloe: Greek, meaning 'green shoot' or 'blooming'. An epithet of the goddess Demeter, also found in the New Testament.
Teodor: Form of Theodore, from Greek 'gift of God'. Common in Romance, Slavic and Scandinavian languages.
Bayan: Arabic, meaning 'clarity' or 'eloquence, explanation'. In Turkic languages it can mean 'lady' or 'rich'.
Meva: Probably Turkish and Kurdish meva, meaning 'fruit'. Origin uncertain.
Jayce: Modern English name, probably a variant of Jace or Jason, from Greek 'healer'. Possibly from the initials J.C.
Ravi: Sanskrit, meaning 'sun'. A common Indian name, also the Sun god in Hindu tradition.
Joachim: Hebrew, meaning 'God will establish'. Traditionally the father of the Virgin Mary.
Nils: Scandinavian short form of Nikolaus (Nicholas), from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Clémentine: French feminine form of Clement, from Latin clemens, meaning 'merciful' or 'mild'.
Marwan: Arabic, probably meaning 'flint' or 'hard stone'. Borne by Umayyad caliphs.
Esma: Turkish and Bosnian form of Asma, from Arabic, meaning 'higher, more exalted'. Also associated with 'names'.
Jonah: Hebrew Yonah, meaning 'dove'. The biblical prophet swallowed by a great fish.
Sena: Probably Turkish, meaning 'praise' or 'brightness'. Also a Ghanaian name and a Japanese surname; origin varies by culture.
Malika: Arabic, meaning 'queen'. Also used in Central Asia and India.
Jibril: Arabic form of Gabriel, the archangel, from Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Edith: Old English Eadgyth, from ead 'wealth, prosperity' and gyth 'war'. Borne by Saint Edith and an English queen.
Zayneb: Variant spelling of Arabic Zaynab, probably 'fragrant tree' or 'father's adornment'. Borne by the Prophet Muhammad's daughter.
Harun: Arabic and Turkish form of Aaron, the brother of Moses. Famous through caliph Harun al-Rashid.
Lotta: Scandinavian and Finnish short form of Charlotte, the French feminine of Charles, from Germanic 'free man'.
Zoe: Greek, meaning 'life'. Early Christians used it as a translation of Hebrew Eve.
Amalya: Variant of Amalia, from the Germanic root amal 'work'. Possibly also linked to Hebrew Amalya 'work of God'.
Abby: English short form of Abigail, from Hebrew, meaning 'my father is joy'.
April: English, from the month, which derives from Latin Aprilis. Possibly linked to aperire 'to open', as in spring buds.
Kassim: Arabic Qasim, meaning 'one who divides or distributes'. Borne by a son of the Prophet Muhammad.
Leonora: Italian and Spanish short form of Eleonora, itself of uncertain origin. Possibly a variant of Helen.
Sama: Arabic, meaning 'sky' or 'heaven'. In Sanskrit, a related name means 'equal, calm'.
Eflin: Turkish, probably a modern coinage meaning 'lunar glow'. Origin uncertain; rare.
Liaz: Rare modern name; probably Arabic or Hebrew-influenced, possibly meaning 'my strength'. Origin uncertain.
Zayan: Arabic and Urdu, meaning 'beauty' or 'adornment'. Also used as 'bright, shining'.
Elior: Hebrew, meaning 'my God is light'. Modern Israeli name.
Ollie: English short form of Oliver or Olivia, from Latin oliva 'olive tree'.
Géraume: French form of Jerome, from Greek Hieronymos, meaning 'sacred name'. Rare archaic spelling.
Emilien: French form of Latin Aemilianus, from the Roman family name Aemilius, probably 'rival' or 'eager'.
Staf: Flemish short form of Gustaaf or Christiaan, possibly Eustaaf. Origin uncertain.
Clarisse: French form of Clare, from Latin clarus 'bright, clear, famous'.
Daphné: French form of Greek Daphne, meaning 'laurel'. In myth, a nymph turned into a laurel tree.
Thaïs: Greek, probably 'bandage' or 'of the Thais region'. Borne by an Athenian courtesan and a Christian saint.
Hasan: Arabic, meaning 'good' or 'handsome'. Borne by the Prophet Muhammad's grandson.
Harold: Old English Hereweald, from here 'army' and weald 'ruler'. Borne by English kings.
Erik: Scandinavian, from Old Norse Eiríkr, meaning 'eternal ruler' or 'sole ruler'.
Abdul: Arabic abd al-, meaning 'servant of the', used in names such as Abdul Rahman.
Ilaria: Italian form of Hilary, from Latin hilaris, meaning 'cheerful'.
Amar: Arabic and Indian name, meaning 'immortal' in Sanskrit and 'builder' or 'long-lived' in Arabic.
Yousef: Arabic form of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Lyanna: Modern name, probably a blend of Lyn and Anna, or a variant of Liana. Popularized by Game of Thrones.
Nélya: Modern French-style coinage, possibly a variant of Nelia or Nelly. Origin uncertain.
Lillie: English diminutive of Lily, from the flower name, or of Elizabeth.
Joppe: Dutch and Flemish, probably a diminutive of Jacob or Joris. Origin uncertain; also linked to Jaffa (Joppa).
Yannis: Greek form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Saar: Dutch, a short form of Sara, from Hebrew 'princess'. Also Hebrew for 'storm'.
Zehra: Turkish form of Arabic Zahra, meaning 'radiant' or 'shining'. Epithet of Fatima.
Marc: French and Catalan form of Mark, from Latin Marcus, probably linked to Mars, the god of war.
Pol: Catalan and Dutch form of Paul, from Latin Paulus, meaning 'small' or 'humble'.
Anaé: Modern French name, probably a variant of Anaïs or Anna, meaning 'grace'. Origin uncertain.
Rim: Arabic, meaning 'white antelope' or 'gazelle'. Also spelled Reem.
Tobe: Flemish short form of Tobias, from Hebrew 'God is good'.
Andrei: Romanian and Russian form of Andrew, from Greek andreios, meaning 'manly, brave'.
Rita: Short form of Margarita, from Greek margarites 'pearl'. Also a saint's name, St. Rita of Cascia.
Salman: Arabic, meaning 'safe' or 'peaceful'. Borne by Salman the Persian, a companion of the Prophet.
Valerio: Italian form of Latin Valerius, from valere, meaning 'to be strong, healthy'.
Camilla: Latin, a Roman family name; possibly meaning 'attendant at a religious ceremony'. In myth, a warrior maiden.
Cosette: French diminutive of Nicolette, from Nicholas. Made famous by Les Misérables.
Riley: English, from an Irish surname meaning 'valiant' or from Old English 'rye clearing'.
Ray: English short form of Raymond, from Germanic 'wise protector'. Also from Old French roy 'king'.
Sultan: Arabic, meaning 'ruler' or 'authority'. Used as both title and given name.
Souleymen: Variant spelling of Suleiman, the Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew 'peace'.
Moon: English word name for the satellite. Also a Korean surname and modern given name.
Samaël: Hebrew in origin, possibly 'God's poison' or 'venom of God'. In tradition, an angel of death; also read as 'God has heard'.
Isao: Japanese, meaning 'merit', 'honor' or 'achievement' depending on the characters used.
Arto: Finnish, possibly a form of Arthur, or Armenian Arto, a short form of Artashes. Origin varies.
Olympe: French form of Greek Olympia, meaning 'of Olympus', the home of the gods.
Gérard: French form of Germanic Gerhard, from ger 'spear' and hard 'brave, hardy'.
Eliora: Hebrew, meaning 'my God is light'. Feminine form of Elior.
Nox: Latin, meaning 'night'. Modern rare given name; also the Roman goddess of night.
Rémy: French form of Latin Remigius, meaning 'oarsman'. Saint Rémy baptized Clovis.
Natan: Hebrew, meaning 'he gave'. The biblical prophet Nathan.
Tiebe: Frisian and Dutch, a form of Tiebbe, from the Germanic root theud 'people'. Origin somewhat uncertain.
Manuel: Spanish and Portuguese, from Hebrew Immanuel, meaning 'God is with us'.
Fay: English, from Old French fae 'fairy', or a short form of Faith. Also Dutch short form of Fabienne or Faye.
Natalia: Latin, meaning 'born at Christmas'. From natalis dies, 'birthday'.
Lasse: Scandinavian short form of Lars, itself from Laurentius, meaning 'from Laurentum' or 'laurel'.
Josefien: Dutch and Flemish form of Josephine, the feminine of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Matz: Low German and Scandinavian short form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Senn: Probably a short form of Senne or a modern coinage. Possibly a variant of Sven. Origin uncertain.
Héléna: French form of Helena, from Greek, usually explained as 'torch' or 'shining light'.
Tille: Dutch and Frisian short form of Mathilde, from Germanic 'strength in battle'.
Daniela: Italian and Spanish feminine of Daniel, from Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Djibril: French West African spelling of Jibril, the archangel Gabriel, from Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Naud: Probably a Dutch short form of Arnaud or Renaud, from Germanic 'ruler' roots. Origin uncertain.
Matilde: Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Matilda, from Germanic 'strength in battle'.
Rebeca: Spanish and Portuguese form of Rebecca, from Hebrew, possibly 'to tie' or 'captivating'.
Agnès: French form of Agnes, from Greek hagne, meaning 'pure'. Often linked with Latin agnus 'lamb'.
Timur: Turkic, meaning 'iron'. Borne by the conqueror Tamerlane.
Boubacar: West African form of Abu Bakr, the first caliph. From Arabic, meaning 'father of the young camel'.
Paola: Italian feminine form of Paul, from Latin Paulus, meaning 'small' or 'humble'.
Lyvia: Modern variant of Livia, from Latin, possibly meaning 'bluish' or 'envious'. Origin uncertain.
Ysée: French form of Iseult or Isolde, perhaps from Celtic or Germanic roots. Origin uncertain.
Odet: French short form of Odette, a diminutive of Oda, from Germanic aud 'wealth, fortune'.
Dries: Dutch short form of Andries, a form of Andrew, from Greek 'manly'.
Sofie: Scandinavian, Dutch and German form of Sophia, from Greek, meaning 'wisdom'.
Chloë: Variant of Chloe, from Greek, meaning 'green shoot' or 'blooming'.
Thibo: Dutch short form of Thibault or Thibaut, from Germanic 'bold people'.
Mikail: Turkish and Arabic form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Esra: Turkish and Arabic form of Ezra, from Hebrew 'help'. Also used in Turkish as a female name.
Ensar: Arabic Ansar, meaning 'helpers'. Refers to the Medina residents who aided the Prophet.
Sila: Turkish, meaning 'homeland' or 'return home'. Also an Inuit name for sky or air.
Louana: Modern blend of Louise and Anna, or of Louis and Ana. Origin uncertain.
Leonor: Spanish and Portuguese form of Eleanor, of uncertain origin; possibly from Provençal Aliénor or Helen.
Rayhana: Arabic, meaning 'sweet basil' or 'fragrant plant'. Also the Prophet's wife Rayhana.
Dahlia: English, from the flower named after Swedish botanist Anders Dahl. Also Hebrew 'branch' in Israel.
Mouhamed: French West African spelling of Muhammad, from Arabic, meaning 'praised'.
Nila: Sanskrit and Tamil, meaning 'blue' or 'dark blue'. Also a Latvian and English diminutive.
Lucía: Spanish form of Lucy, from Latin lux, meaning 'light'.
Khaled: Arabic Khalid, meaning 'eternal' or 'immortal'. Borne by the general Khalid ibn al-Walid.
Ares: Greek, the god of war. Possibly from Greek 'ruin' or 'bane'. Also a rare Catalan given name.
Luqman: Arabic, a wise man in the Quran. Origin uncertain; possibly from Hebrew or Ethiopic roots.
Willow: English, from the tree. A modern nature name associated with flexibility and grace.
Aren: Probably Armenian or Scandinavian. Possibly from Old Norse 'eagle' or a variant of Aaron. Origin uncertain.
Raya: Arabic and Hebrew meaning 'friend'. Also Slavic short form of Raisa or Rajna.
Milann: Modern spelling of Milan, from Slavic mil 'gracious, dear'. Also an Italian city name.
Enea: Italian form of Aeneas, the Trojan hero. From Greek 'praised'.
Dawud: Arabic form of David, from Hebrew, meaning 'beloved'.
Ro: Short form of Rose, Roland or Robin. Also Japanese 'wave'. Origin varies.
Mirthe: Dutch form of Myrtle, from Greek myrtos, the myrtle plant, symbol of love.
Reda: Arabic Rida, meaning 'contentment' or 'satisfaction'. Also a Lithuanian name of uncertain origin.
Ysaline: French, probably a variant of Isaline or Isabelle from Hebrew 'God is my oath'. Origin uncertain; possibly an Iseult form.
Pepijn: Dutch form of Pepin, a Frankish name of uncertain origin. Borne by Pepin the Short.
Nada: Arabic, meaning 'dew' or 'generosity'. In Slavic languages, it means 'hope'.
Achraf: Arabic Ashraf, meaning 'most honorable' or 'noblest'. Maghrebi French spelling.
Giuseppe: Italian form of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Maja: Scandinavian and Slavic form of Maya or Maria. Linked to Latin Maia, goddess of spring, or to Mary.
Cléa: French form of Clea, a short form of Cleopatra or Clelia. From Greek kleos, meaning 'glory'.
Antoni: Catalan and Polish form of Anthony, from the Roman family name Antonius, of uncertain meaning.
Néo: French form of Neo, from Greek neos meaning 'new'. Popularized by The Matrix.
Miraç: Turkish, meaning 'ascension', referring to Muhammad's night ascension to heaven. From Arabic miraj.
Connor: Anglicized Irish Conchobhar, possibly meaning 'lover of hounds' or 'wolf lover'.
Eléanore: French variant of Eleanor, of uncertain origin; possibly from Provençal Aliénor or Helen.
Baran: Turkish and Kurdish, meaning 'rain'. Also a Polish surname meaning 'ram'.
Augustine: French feminine of Augustin, from Latin augustus, meaning 'venerable' or 'majestic'.
Paloma: Spanish, meaning 'dove', the symbol of peace.
Hussein: Arabic, a diminutive of Hasan, meaning 'good' or 'handsome'. Borne by the Prophet's grandson.
Giuliana: Italian feminine form of Julian, from Latin Julianus, from the Roman family name Julius.
Fynn: Variant of Finn, from Irish Fionn 'fair' or Old Norse Finnr 'Sami'. Also Frisian.
Ilay: Turkish, meaning 'moonlight' or 'halo of the moon'. Also a Hebrew-influenced variant.
Bill: English short form of William, from Germanic 'will' and 'helmet'.
Teodora: Italian, Spanish and Slavic feminine of Theodore, from Greek 'gift of God'.
Shams: Arabic, meaning 'sun'. Also used as a name in Persian.
Iqra: Arabic, meaning 'read' or 'recite'. The first word revealed to Muhammad in the Quran.
Maximilien: French form of Maximilian, from Latin Maximus 'greatest' and Aemilianus; possibly a blend coined by Emperor Frederick III.
Giovanni: Italian form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
John: English form of Latin Johannes, from Hebrew Yochanan, meaning 'God is gracious'.
Francesco: Italian form of Francis, from Latin Franciscus, meaning 'Frenchman' or 'free man'.
Samira: Arabic, meaning 'companion in evening conversation'. Also Sanskrit-linked 'breeze'.
Fenne: Dutch and Frisian, a short form of Josefien or Fenna. Possibly from Germanic 'fen'. Origin uncertain.
Othman: Arabic Uthman, probably meaning 'baby bustard'. Borne by the third caliph.
Aurelia: Latin, meaning 'golden'. Feminine of the Roman family name Aurelius.
Catalina: Spanish form of Catherine, from Greek, perhaps meaning 'pure'.
Arianna: Italian form of Ariadne, from Greek, meaning 'most holy' or 'very pure'.
Cecilia: Latin feminine of Caecilius, probably 'blind' or 'dim-sighted'. Saint Cecilia patronizes musicians.
Ramon: Catalan and Spanish form of Raymond, from Germanic 'wise protector'.
Jace: Modern English, a variant of Jason, from Greek 'healer'. Also used from the initials J.C.
Mattheo: Variant of Matteo, the Italian form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Mahmoud: Arabic Mahmud, meaning 'praised' or 'commendable', from the same root as Muhammad.
Giselle: French, from Germanic gisil, meaning 'pledge' or 'hostage'. Also a ballet title.
Sare: Probably a variant of Sara, from Hebrew 'princess'. Also a Basque place name.
Rover: English word name, meaning 'wanderer'. Rare as a given name; also a dog name.
Dunya: Arabic, meaning 'world' or 'worldly life'. Also a Russian short form of Avdotya.
Leano: Modern coinage, probably from Leo or Leandro. Origin uncertain.
Emrys: Welsh form of Ambrose, from Greek ambrosios, meaning 'immortal'. Merlin is also called Myrddin Emrys.
Elara: Greek, a nymph, mother of Tityos in myth. Also a moon of Jupiter. Meaning uncertain.
Dorian: Greek, meaning 'from Doris', an ancient Greek region. Popularized by The Picture of Dorian Gray.
Sien: Dutch short form of Rosina or Katharina. Also from Mathilde or Josina.
Elyne: Modern variant of Eline or Eveline, Dutch forms of Aveline or Helen. Origin uncertain.
Ilario: Italian form of Hilary, from Latin hilaris, meaning 'cheerful'.
Grace: English, from Latin gratia, meaning 'grace' or 'favor'. A Christian virtue name.
Naëlle: Modern French variant of Noëlle, from Latin natalis, meaning 'birth', hence 'Christmas'.
